titleZh: 农民视角：为何投资无人机
summaryZh: 在2026年Farm Progress Show上，无人机成为焦点。爱荷华州农民Robbie Gustin分享了他购买两台DJI T100无人机的实践经验，用于自家玉米大豆田的杀菌剂、杀虫剂施用及覆盖作物播种。他投资的核心动机是将农事作业留在农场内部，摆脱对外包服务的依赖，实现按需及时作业。文章提供了设备成本（每台约4.5万美元）、回本周期（两年）及新手建议，对考虑引入无人机技术的大田种植者具有实操参考价值。
featuredReason: 本文通过一线农民的真实使用案例，展示了植保无人机在大田作物上的实际应用价值与投资回报逻辑，为智慧农业领域的从业者提供了接地气的实践参考。

Farmer POV: Why invest in a drone

Farm Progress Show: In attempts to keep applications on the farm, one farmer bought two drones. Learn about which type of drones he invested in and how he’s using them on his operation.

Ava Splear,Staff Writer, Prairie Farmer September 2, 2026

schedule2 Min Read

At the 2026 Farm Progress Show, attendees can watch various drones fly over fields. TV screens inside the tent display the pilot’s real-time view. Gil Gullickson 

Subscribe to Farm Progress AGTech — our free, twice-weekly newsletter delivering the latest innovations, emerging technologies and expert insights to your inbox.

Drones are making a big appearance at this year’s Farm Progress Show — both in the Drone Zone and as companies display their new models.

Robbie Gustin, Ute, Iowa, farmer, has incorporated this emerging technology into his operation to keep money in his pocket instead of paying someone else to make applications.

Gustin, who grows corn and soybeans with his father-in-law, bought two DGI T100 drones and used them for the first time this year to apply fungicides and insecticides on his farm.

He also experimented with using the drones to apply cover crops, including oats and rye, flying the cover crop seed into the standing crop.

Why make the investment into drones? Gustin said it was a step toward keeping all services in-house.

“I had a helicopter doing it before. Everything else we do on the farm ourselves, and we thought, ‘Why not give it a try and try to keep everything on the farm?’” he said.

Related:Favorite products from FPS26

Plus, this allows for timely applications that aren’t dependent on wet weather or a hired company’s schedule.

“We’re doing it on our schedule and scouting fields and hitting it at the right time,” Gustin said.

This year he made mostly single fungicide applications in corn, with a couple of two-pass applications. Overall, he said disease pressure hasn’t been heavy on his western Iowa farm this year.

Gustin said the next piece of drone equipment he’s considering is a camera drone for more accurate mapping features, for things like tree lines.

Within two years total, Gustin expects to have paid off both drones — which cost about $45,000 each.

He’s thought about custom work, but since this was his first year with the drone, he wanted to focus on his own farm.

Gustin emphasized that introducing drones into your operation involves a learning curve. His advice for those considering drone technology?

“Do your research and make a good decision on what’s going to be best for you, because it’s a big investment,” he said.

About the Author

Ava Splear

Staff Writer, Prairie Farmer 

Growing up on her family’s grain farm in northern Illinois, Ava Splear decided to pursue a career that links her upbringing around agriculture with her passion for communication and storytelling. While a student at the University of Illinois, Ava was involved in Agricultural Communicators of Tomorrow, serving as its president. During her time in school, she gained professional experience through internships with DeKalb County Farm Bureau, John Deere and Ideal Industries, as well as the university's College of Agricultural, Consumer and Environmental Sciences in marketing communications. Graduating in 2024, with a degree in agricultural leadership, education and communications, Ava returned to northern Illinois to work for Farm Progress.

translationZh:
在2026年Farm Progress Show上，无人机在展会上大放异彩——无论是在无人机专区，还是各公司展示的新机型中，都随处可见。

爱荷华州尤特市的农民Robbie Gustin已将这项新兴技术融入他的农场运营，目的是把钱留在自己口袋里，而不是花钱请别人来做施药作业。

Gustin与他的岳父一起种植玉米和大豆。他购买了两台DJI T100无人机，今年首次使用它们在自己的农田上施用杀菌剂和杀虫剂。

他还尝试用无人机播撒覆盖作物种子，包括燕麦和黑麦，将覆盖作物种子撒播进尚未收获的 standing crop（站立作物）中。

为什么要投资无人机？Gustin表示，这是朝着将所有服务留在农场内部迈出的一步。

“以前我是雇直升机来做这件事。农场上的其他所有工作都是我们自己完成的，我们想，‘为什么不试试，尽量把所有事情都留在农场里做呢？’”他说。

此外，这还能实现及时施药，不受潮湿天气或外包公司日程安排的限制。

“我们按自己的日程安排作业，自己巡查田地，在正确的时间节点进行操作，”Gustin说。

今年，他在玉米上主要进行了单次杀菌剂施用，也有几次两次施用的作业。总体而言，他表示今年他所在的西爱荷华州农场病害压力并不严重。

Gustin表示，他接下来考虑添置的无人机设备是一台摄像无人机，用于获取更精准的测绘功能，比如用于测绘树线等。

Gustin预计，在两年内，这两架无人机——每架成本约45,000美元——将全部回本。

他也考虑过提供定制服务，但由于今年是他使用无人机的第一年，他想先专注于自家农场。

Gustin强调，将无人机引入你的农场运营需要一个学习过程。他对那些考虑采用无人机技术的人的建议是：

“做好功课，做出最适合自己的明智决定，因为这是一笔很大的投资。”
